title: Just Talk Once: Communication-Efficient Split Federated LLM Fine-Tuning on Edge Devices
journal: ACM International Symposium on Theory, Algorithmic Foundations, and Protocol Design for Mobile Networks and Mobile Computing (MobiHoc)
abstract: Large language model (LLM) fine-tuning is increasingly shifting toward data generated on edge devices, where memory, computation, bandwidth, and connectivity constraints make conventional federated learning difficult to sustain. Split federated fine-tuning (SFT) improves client-side efficiency by offloading most model parameters and computation to the server but requires step-by-step bidirectional communication loop across the split interface and forces continuous client involvement throughout training. In this paper, we present L-shaped SFT, a split fine-tuning framework that removes this bidirectional bottleneck. Our key insight is that weight tying in modern LLMs enables server-side hidden activations to be directly supervised using target embeddings, allowing the training loss to be computed on the server without returning server outputs to the client. To further eliminate the need for continuous client participation, based on L-shaped SFT, we introduce one-shot SFT, in which clients upload activations once and then go offline while the server continues optimization over cached representations. We implement our design in a real system testbed with heterogeneous edge clients, including commercial smartphones and NVIDIA developer boards. Experiments demonstrate that our schemes significantly reduce communication costs and client online time compared with existing SFT baselines.

title: Beyond interpersonal disputes: a text network analysis of conflict and negative communication experiences among experienced nurses
abstract: Background Experienced nurses are defined in this study as nurses with at least two years of clinical experience. They deliver direct patient care, educate junior staff, and coordinate teams. Conflict and negative communication involving this group have been linked to burnout, turnover, and compromised patient safety, yet the semantic structure of these experiences remains poorly understood. Conflict serves here as a conceptual frame, not a separately measured outcome. This study aims to identify core keywords and the semantic structure of these experiences using text network analysis (TNA). Methods The dataset comprised 1,116 free-text narrative entries from 392 experienced nurses across 14 sessions of a Positive Organizational Culture Workshop (August 2021–February 2023) at a tertiary general hospital in South Korea. After preprocessing with three user-defined dictionaries, a co-occurrence network of adjacent terms within sentences (window size two) was constructed in NetMiner 4.5.1.e. The 30 most frequent keywords formed a network of 161 links; after links occurring only once were removed, 86 links remained. Degree, closeness, and betweenness centrality and modularity-based communities were computed on this binary, undirected network, and sensitivity to these two settings was examined. Results Four keywords ranked within the top five on all three centrality measures: “physician in charge,” “phone call,” “family member,” and “senior nurse.” Community detection (modularity = 0.24) suggested five exploratory semantic communities: repeated explanation and complaints from family members; anger and shouting directed at the primary nurse over the phone; orders, verification, and requests involving the physician in charge and other departments; verbal abuse and irritation when reporting to the on-call physician; and hierarchy, handover, and reprimand among nurses. Labels were assigned after reviewing the original narratives. The two highest-ranked keywords in degree centrality were unchanged across alternative settings, whereas community membership varied. Conclusions The reported experiences were structured around telephone-mediated communication with the physician in charge, explanation demands and complaints from patients’ family members, and hierarchical relationships among nurses. The perceived repetition of such experiences was embedded in the family-related community. These concepts may warrant organizational attention in conflict management, and their value as intervention targets remains to be tested. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Barriers to the integration of mental health services into HIV and TB care: a mixed-methods assessment in high-volume healthcare facilities in Niger State, Nigeria
abstract: Background HIV and tuberculosis (TB) remain major public health challenges in Sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in Nigeria, where mental health disorders such as depression and anxiety further compromise adherence to antiretroviral therapy (ART) and directly observed therapy (DOT). Despite this, mental health services remain poorly integrated into healthcare delivery. This baseline assessment evaluated the availability and integration of mental health services in selected facilities in Niger state, in line with Nigeria's national mental health policies. Method A mixed-method cross-sectional design was employed, using cluster sampling to select six facilities across the state and purposive sampling to identify those with the highest ART client load. Quantitative data were collected using assessment checklists and service utilization records, while qualitative data were obtained through key informant interviews (KIIs) with heads of ART, DOT, and Mental Health units. Quantitative analysis using STATA generated percentages, and qualitative data were thematically analyzed. Results Findings showed no integration of mental health services within ART and DOT units across all facilities (0%). Only 25% of facilities had a dedicated mental health desk, adequate workforce, data capturing tools, or safe counselling space. Mental health policies and SOPs (6.3%) and dedicated budgets (6.3%) were largely absent. Referral directories (25%), inter-facility partnerships (12.5%), and support groups (12.5%) were also limited. Overall, the results indicate weak structural readiness and lack of integration of mental health services within HIV and TB care settings. Conclusion The study highlights a critical gap in mental health service integration within HIV and TB care. Considering the rate of professionals compared to demands, training and task-shifting approaches will help expand service delivery, integration of routine screening tools into ART and DOT clinics and strengthening of referral systems through structured directories and digital linkage mechanisms. In addition, tele-mental health support systems are recommended to improve access and continuity of care.

title: Esterified Banana Peel Waste as a Low-Cost Biosorbent for Heavy Metal Removal from Real Paint Manufacturing Wastewater: Effects of Concentration, pH, Contact Time, Dosage, and Regeneration
abstract: The discharge of heavy metal-laden effluents from paint manufacturing operations is a significant and growing environmental hazard in industrialising economies, yet few biosorption studies test authentic multi-metal industrial effluent rather than synthetic single-metal solutions. This study investigates methanol/hydrochloric acid esterified banana peel waste (E-BPW) as a zero-cost biosorbent for removing chromium, nickel, cobalt, and lead from real paint manufacturing wastewater sourced from Brighto Paints Limited, Lahore, Pakistan. E-BPW was prepared by collection, drying, Tyler-standard sieve fractionation (850–1180 µm), and Fischer esterification with methanol and hydrochloric acid at 60°C for 48 h. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed carboxyl, hydroxyl, and ester carbonyl groups as the principal metal-binding moieties. Batch adsorption experiments evaluated the effects of initial metal concentration, solution pH, contact time, and adsorbent dosage, with metal concentrations quantified by flame atomic absorption spectroscopy. Under optimised conditions (pH 6–8, 80 min, 5 g·L⁻¹, 25°C), E-BPW achieved removal efficiencies of 80.3% (Cr), 68.9% (Co), 63.1% (Pb), and 56.0% (Ni). Regeneration with 2 mol·L⁻¹ HNO₃ recovered 99.3% of adsorbed metals, indicating strong potential for circular reuse. These findings demonstrate that waste-to-resource valorisation of agricultural byproducts can deliver technically effective, low-cost heavy metal removal for small-to-medium industrial applications, supporting Sustainable Development Goal 6 and circular-economy principles. The absence of isotherm, kinetic, and surface-characterisation data is acknowledged as a limitation, and a research agenda toward pilot-scale validation is proposed.

title: The quality management system in medical laboratories: seventeen years of strengthening laboratory management towards ISO 15189 accreditation in Tanzania
abstract: Background Recent advances in development and changes in laboratory technology seen in modern medicine have increased the demand on timely, accurate, reliable, and reproducible laboratory results. In public health settings, the laboratory plays a key role in disease surveillance for early detection and confirmation of disease outbreaks. We aimed to describe and document the 15189 accreditation in Tanzania. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study involving databases for medical laboratories in the Ministry of Health and African Society for Laboratory Medicine (ASLM). All laboratories which participated in quality management system in Tanzania were included in the study from national to health centre levels. Results Out of 157 laboratories implementing QMS from 2007 to 2024, a total of 81 (51.6%) laboratories were accredited. Secondary laboratory level had high number of enrolments into QMS program 117 (74.5%) followed by tertiary laboratories 26 (16.6%). The proportion of accredited laboratories at tertiary level was (73.1%) (p < 0.033) which was significantly higher compared to other levels. There was significantly higher proportion of laboratories accredited through direct laboratory accreditation process 25/28, (89.3%), compared with SLMTA program 59/129 (44.4%) (p < 0.001 ). There was a significant increase of accredited laboratories among SLMTA program from 1/76 (1.3%) in 2017 to 56/157 (35.7%) in 2024, ( p = 0.027) compared to direct laboratory accreditation approach. Conclusions Laboratory accreditation is a hallmark of quality management system implementation which can be achieved either through direct laboratory accreditation approach or the SLMTA program. The seventeen years of experience in implementing QMS indicates that the SLMTA program is more efficient, effectiveness and user-friendly than the direct laboratory accreditation approach.
